title: Sylvan Dynamics - API time-to-first-inference & privacy pathfinder
summary: Intro discovery covering Sylvan's ML roadmap, strict data residency needs, and questions about time-to-first-inference. Redwood AE + SE walked through hosted vs dedicated vs private options, security controls, expected pilot flow and metrics for acceptance.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-22 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (CTO), Devon Park (Lead ML Eng), Alex Chen (Security PM)

Auto-generated Summary: quick discovery, strong privacy requirements, leaning toward Private or Dedicated with VPC depending on latency/cost.

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm jordan with redwood inference, priya is our solutions engineer. quick roll call?
[00:18] Marta (Sylvan): hi, this is marta, sylvan cto. we have devon and alex on, thanks for the invite.
[00:28] Devon (Sylvan): hey, devon here, lead ml eng. focusing on customer-facing agents and content moderation flows.
[00:38] Alex (Sylvan): alex, security program manager. here to scope compliance and key management stuff.
[00:45] Jordan (Redwood AE): awesome. rough agenda: time-to-first-inference for a pilot, data residency and kms/ssO questions, and hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs. also we'll share a pilot benchmark template. sound good?
[01:05] Marta (Sylvan): yep. our timeline is tight, hoping to have a pilot in january, low-latency interactive use case, mostly eu-resident customers.
[01:22] Priya (Redwood SE): quick Q: what are your p95 latency targets and expected qps for the pilot?
[01:30] Devon (Sylvan): target p95 ~200-300ms for short chat completions, concurrent users maybe 50-100, but bursty. cost is also a factor, we can't overspend.
[01:48] Jordan (Redwood AE): cool. so redswood hosted api can get you to first call in hours — free credits -> quickstart. dedicated gives more predictability and reserved throughput, private (vpc/on-prem) addresses strict residency and key control.
[02:10] Alex (Sylvan): can you clarify kms/hsm integration for private? we need customer-managed keys and audit logs across all requests.
[02:23] Priya (Redwood SE): yes — private includes bring-your-own-kms options, HSM-backed key stores, and we push audit logs to your SIEM. hosted can be configured with customer key wrapping for certain tiers but less isolated than private. (there's some background noise)
[02:52] Marta (Sylvan): okay, and SOC2, ISO? we need attestation before pilot.
[02:58] Jordan (Redwood AE): we have SOC2 Type II and ISO-27001 docs we can share. i'll attach the compliance pack.
[03:12] Devon (Sylvan): on the perf side, what about batching/kv cache? our prompts often reuse prefixes — caching would help cost and tail latency.
[03:25] Priya (Redwood SE): yup. runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching, automatic batching heuristics. we can tune batch windows to trade latency vs throughput. we also have quantization suggestions for cost. note: sometimes the auto-transcription says "K V cash" which is wrong but the feature is KV cache.
[03:50] Jordan (Redwood AE): worth noting: for pilot we'd recommend hosted for fastest ttfi, then a dedicated reserved pool if you need throughput, and private if you need strict residency and KMS. we'd typically run a short benchmark to compare hosted-latency vs dedicated for your workload.
[04:15] Devon (Sylvan): how long does a dedicated ramp take? we're on a january timeline.
[04:22] Jordan (Redwood AE): provisioning a dedicated pool can take 2-4 weeks depending on capacity and contracts; hosted is immediate; private on VPC can be 3-6 weeks including network setup and security review.
[04:38] Alex (Sylvan): network wise, do you support privateLink equivalents? we use aws privatelink and strict egress rules.
[04:45] Priya (Redwood SE): yes, we support AWS PrivateLink, GCP VPC peering, and on-prem connectors. for private deployments we can run inside your VPC.
[04:58] Marta (Sylvan): about pricing — are token prices public? how do we estimate cost for 100k monthly tokens?
[05:07] Jordan (Redwood AE): i'll send a cost worksheet; quick rule of thumb depends on model choice (open models vs optimized variants), and quantization can drop costs. we'll include estimates in the pricing doc.
[05:20] Devon (Sylvan): also need to validate model outputs — how do you do quality regressions and evals?
[05:28] Priya (Redwood SE): Redwood Optimize can run evals tied to prompt sets, quality monitoring, and regression alerts. for pilot we can set up a small eval harness to track F1/accuracy or a human-in-the-loop check.
[05:45] Jordan (Redwood AE): any blockers from your side for starting the hosted pilot with free credits?
[05:52] Marta (Sylvan): primary blocker is data residency and legal signoff. if hosted can be restricted to eu region and we get data retention terms, maybe ok. otherwise we might need private.
[06:07] Alex (Sylvan): need written commitments on data deletion and auditability before internal approval.
[06:15] Jordan (Redwood AE): understood. we have regional hosting options and retention SLAs; i'll share the data processing addendum.
[06:25] Devon (Sylvan): for latency benchmarks, can you run something with our sample prompt set? we want realistic token distributions.
[06:33] Priya (Redwood SE): absolutely — send the prompt set and we'll run hosted vs dedicated runs, measure p50/p95, throughput, and cost.
[06:44] Marta (Sylvan): what's the expected hands-on support? we might need SE time to tune batching, model selection, and rollout policy.
[06:52] Jordan (Redwood AE): pilot includes a short SE engagement; we can allocate a couple days for benchmarks and tuning. for dedicated/private deployments we'd include more runway and ops support.
[07:02] Devon (Sylvan): okay. one more — can you do canary rollouts between model variants? we plan to A/B test a quantized faster model vs a higher-quality model.
[07:12] Priya (Redwood SE): yes, rollouts and automatic fallback policies are supported in the console; we can route traffic by model version and set rollback thresholds.
[07:22] Alex (Sylvan): security question: do you provide token-level tracing for auditing?
[07:28] Jordan (Redwood AE): yes, token-level cost and trace hooks are available in Redwood Console, and we can forward traces to your tracing backend.
[07:37] Marta (Sylvan): great. next steps?
[07:40] Jordan (Redwood AE): i'll summarize: 1) send compliance pack and DPA, 2) send pricing + pilot SOW, 3) Priya to run benchmarks once you share prompt set, 4) schedule a follow-up in one week.
[07:58] Devon (Sylvan): can we get the pilot SOW with a 2-week hosted benchmark then an option to move to dedicated?
[08:05] Jordan (Redwood AE): yes. we'll draft a SOW with milestone gating based on benchmark results.
[08:12] Alex (Sylvan): i'll review the compliance pack and come back with any gaps.
[08:18] Marta (Sylvan): sounds good, thanks.
[08:22] Jordan (Redwood AE): thanks all — any final questions?
[08:25] Devon (Sylvan): none from me.
[08:27] Alex (Sylvan): none.
[08:30] Jordan (Redwood AE): cool, we'll follow up with links and docs.

(Background chatter and brief crosstalk at times; occasional transcription mistakes — e.g., "privatized" for private, "K V cash" for KV cache.)
